question: Which AI agents create the most value?
html:
Which AI agents create the most value?

At the agent level, the context does not say. The data shown points to Thomas Scientific and Frontline agents, and to the wave-three revenue agents, as the largest pools. The program totals about $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent value (est.) (Portfolio AI-agent plan, Oct 6, 2026).

Value by portfolio company

Portfolio companyEst. annual valueShare of total (est.)
Thomas Scientific$3.84M~30%
Frontline$3.59M~28%
BPI$2.27M~18%
CET$1.32M~10%
Punctual Pros$0.88M~7%
Fair Harbor$0.77M~6%
  • Thomas Scientific and Frontline together hold about 59% of the estimated value (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • Each company total sits inside its range in the ServiceOS evidence roadmap (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Value by rollout wave

  • Wave 3, revenue agents: $4.19M est., the largest wave.
  • Wave 2, finance agents: $3.91M est.
  • Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents: $2.81M est. This wave has the clearest baselines and lowest risk.
  • Wave 4, monitoring services: $1.77M est.

Source for all four: Portfolio AI-agent plan.

Strongest single-agent evidence

  • The only agent with a worked model is the Punctual Pros missed-call and after-hours booking agent, which is in wave 1.
  • That model recovers about $1.37M a year of jobs (est.): $390k after-hours plus $982k daytime and storm overflow (Voice AI research).
  • Outbound member renewal adds about $403k (est.) on an assumed 6,000 members (Voice AI research).
  • These figures are revenue, not EBITDA. They cannot be compared directly with the $0.88M EBITDA-equivalent figure for Punctual Pros (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Caveats

  • Every value is an analyst assumption. Volumes such as calls, tickets, invoices and members are estimates, not system-of-record counts (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • The totals are not de-duplicated, so agents may double-count shared gains (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
  • Many metric claims come from vendor case studies and are self-reported (Voice AI research).
  • Only 2 of 61 agent items are visible here. A ranking needs the estimated-value field for all 61 agents.

Next actions

  1. Pull the estimated annual value for all 61 agents and rank them. Start with Thomas Scientific and Frontline.
  2. Replace the analyst volumes with system-of-record counts at Thomas Scientific, Frontline and Punctual Pros. This covers call logs, tickets, invoices and member counts.
  3. De-duplicate overlapping agent value before any figure goes into a growth plan or board materials.
  4. Convert the Punctual Pros missed-call revenue estimate to an EBITDA basis using company margin data. Then reconcile it with the agent plan figure.

# Which AI agents create the most value?

At the agent level, the context does not say. The data shown points to Thomas Scientific and Frontline agents, and to the wave-three revenue agents, as the largest pools. The program totals about $12.7M a year of run-rate EBITDA-equivalent value (est.) (Portfolio AI-agent plan, Oct 6, 2026).

## Value by portfolio company

| Portfolio company | Est. annual value | Share of total (est.) |
|---|---|---|
| Thomas Scientific | $3.84M | ~30% |
| Frontline | $3.59M | ~28% |
| BPI | $2.27M | ~18% |
| CET | $1.32M | ~10% |
| Punctual Pros | $0.88M | ~7% |
| Fair Harbor | $0.77M | ~6% |

- Thomas Scientific and Frontline together hold about 59% of the estimated value (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
- Each company total sits inside its range in the ServiceOS evidence roadmap (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Value by rollout wave

- **Wave 3, revenue agents:** $4.19M est., the largest wave.
- **Wave 2, finance agents:** $3.91M est.
- **Wave 1, inbound-contact and document agents:** $2.81M est. This wave has the clearest baselines and lowest risk.
- **Wave 4, monitoring services:** $1.77M est.

Source for all four: Portfolio AI-agent plan.

## Strongest single-agent evidence

- The only agent with a worked model is the Punctual Pros missed-call and after-hours booking agent, which is in wave 1.
- That model recovers about $1.37M a year of jobs (est.): $390k after-hours plus $982k daytime and storm overflow (Voice AI research).
- Outbound member renewal adds about $403k (est.) on an assumed 6,000 members (Voice AI research).
- These figures are revenue, not EBITDA. They cannot be compared directly with the $0.88M EBITDA-equivalent figure for Punctual Pros (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

## Caveats

- Every value is an analyst assumption. Volumes such as calls, tickets, invoices and members are estimates, not system-of-record counts (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
- The totals are not de-duplicated, so agents may double-count shared gains (Portfolio AI-agent plan).
- Many metric claims come from vendor case studies and are self-reported (Voice AI research).
- Only 2 of 61 agent items are visible here. A ranking needs the estimated-value field for all 61 agents.

## Next actions

1. Pull the estimated annual value for all 61 agents and rank them. Start with Thomas Scientific and Frontline.
2. Replace the analyst volumes with system-of-record counts at Thomas Scientific, Frontline and Punctual Pros. This covers call logs, tickets, invoices and member counts.
3. De-duplicate overlapping agent value before any figure goes into a growth plan or board materials.
4. Convert the Punctual Pros missed-call revenue estimate to an EBITDA basis using company margin data. Then reconcile it with the agent plan figure.
